questions.stem: A company handles each incident competently but never meets afterward, and the same weaknesses keep causing repeat incidents. What BEST describes the gap?

options.rationale: Correct: incident handling is a lifecycle; learning feeds preparation.
Speed isn't described as a problem.
A guess; the gap is the missing feedback.

questions.explanation: Incident handling is the overall process of preparing for, detecting, responding to, and learning from incidents. It runs as a lifecycle, not a one-time event.
questions.discriminator_tested: A lifecycle, not a one-time event.

questions.stem: Which two entries in the log below are security incidents rather than ordinary events? (Choose two.)
questions.exhibit:
09:00  User jlee logged in (VPN)
09:14  AV quarantined EICAR test file (scheduled test)
09:31  Firewall blocked inbound scan from 203.0.113.9
09:47  HR database exported to unknown external host
09:52  Ransom note found on file server FS-03
questions.explanation: Security incidents are events that violate or threaten security policy or harm confidentiality, integrity, or availability. An event is any observable occurrence; an incident is an event with an adverse effect.
questions.discriminator_tested: An incident is an event with an adverse effect.

questions.stem: What BEST explains why a company should set its ransomware payment policy before any ransomware incident?

options.rationale: Correct: a pre-set policy avoids panic decisions.

questions.explanation: A ransomware incident encrypts data for payment. The response relies on isolation, backups, and a pre-set payment policy.

questions.stem: A visitor in a hi-vis vest follows staff through a secure door, then asks the receptionist for the Wi-Fi password and is given it. What type of incident is this?

options.rationale: Correct: people manipulated into giving access.
The visitor has no legitimate access.

questions.explanation: A social engineering incident is one where people are manipulated into giving access or information. The response includes credential resets (here, the Wi-Fi password) and user education.

questions.stem: Several staff report the email below. What is the BEST first response?
questions.exhibit:
From:     IT Support <it-support@micros0ft-help.com>
Subject:  Your password expires today
Body:     Keep your access: hxxp://micros0ft-help[.]com/reset

options.rationale: Correct: stops more people falling for it.

questions.explanation: A phishing incident uses fraudulent messages to steal credentials or deliver malware. Report it, block the sender and URLs, and reset any exposed credentials.

questions.stem: What BEST distinguishes a DDoS incident from a denial-of-service attack launched from one host?

options.text: It is blocked by one ACL entry

questions.explanation: A DDoS incident is a flood of traffic from many sources that exhausts a resource. Mitigation often needs upstream help from the ISP.

questions.stem: A vendor announces that one of its software updates shipped with a backdoor. A company installed that update last month. What is the BEST first step?

options.rationale: Drastic, and doesn't find what the backdoor touched.

questions.explanation: Supply chain attacks deliver compromise through a trusted vendor, software update, or component. They arrive through a trusted third party, so they are hard to detect.
questions.discriminator_tested: Compromise via a trusted third party.

questions.stem: An employee with legitimate database access sells customer records. The perimeter firewall and IDS raised no alerts. What BEST explains why?
questions.explanation: Insider threats are harm from someone with legitimate access. The response includes access revocation and monitoring.
questions.discriminator_tested: Harm from someone with legitimate access.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN benefit of incident response planning?

options.rationale: Correct: plans, teams, tools, and policies exist beforehand.

questions.explanation: Incident response planning means preparing plans, teams, tools, and policies before incidents occur. It is done in advance, not during the incident.

questions.stem: During an incident, responders ask who to escalate to and how. The company's IR policy says the CSIRT has authority to act, but nothing more. What document is MOST clearly missing?

options.text: A support contract with a vendor

questions.explanation: An incident response plan is the documented roadmap of roles, procedures, communication, and escalation. Plan = procedures; policy = authority and requirements.

questions.stem: A company's CSIRT is made up of network and server engineers. During a breach, nobody can approve customer notices or advise on legal duties. What is MOST clearly missing?
questions.explanation: A CSIRT (Computer Security Incident Response Team) is the group that handles incidents. It is cross-functional and includes non-technical roles: legal, HR, communications, management.

questions.stem: Which statement from an IR plan BEST shows specifically defined responsibilities?

options.text: The CISO decides; the PR lead speaks
options.rationale: Correct: named roles assigned in advance.

options.text: The team will decide roles then
Roles follow seniority on the day

questions.explanation: Specifically defined responsibilities mean each person's role is assigned in advance: who decides, who communicates, who acts. Clear roles prevent gaps and duplicated effort.

questions.stem: A cyberattack has taken down order processing. What is the MAIN goal of the business continuity section of the IR plan in this situation?

options.rationale: Stale data, and recovery rather than continuity.

questions.explanation: The business continuity plan in the IR plan keeps critical business functions running during an incident. It is business-wide continuity.

questions.stem: Which two belong in an incident communications plan? (Choose two.)

options.rationale: Correct: if normal channels are compromised.

questions.explanation: A communications plan defines who is informed, how, when, and by whom, internally and externally. It uses a designated spokesperson, and backup channels matter if normal ones are compromised.

questions.stem: Each responder records incident notes in a personal style and local time zone. What is the MAIN risk?

options.rationale: Correct: consistency makes timelines and evidence reliable.

options.text: Notes may be lost or deleted
options.rationale: A storage issue, not a format issue.

questions.explanation: Specifically defined documentation standards are consistent templates and formats for recording incident details. Consistency makes timelines and evidence reliable.

questions.stem: Two merged companies use different names for incident phases, which causes confusion in joint exercises. What BEST fixes this?

options.rationale: Correct: a common set of phases and terms.

questions.explanation: Incident response frameworks give structured guidance for organizing incident response. Frameworks give a common set of phases and terms.
questions.discriminator_tested: Frameworks give common phases and terms.

questions.stem: A team's process treats isolating hosts, removing malware, and restoring systems as three separate steps. Which model does this match?

options.rationale: Correct: it separates containment, eradication, and recovery.

questions.explanation: SANS uses six steps: preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery, lessons learned. It separates containment, eradication, and recovery.

questions.stem: What BEST describes NIST's role in incident response?
questions.explanation: NIST is the US standards body whose publications guide incident response. It provides the four-phase lifecycle commonly tested.

questions.stem: In the NIST SP 800-61 (Rev. 2) lifecycle, which phase comes right after detection and analysis?

options.rationale: SANS wording, and it precedes containment.

questions.explanation: NIST SP 800-61 (Rev. 2): preparation; detection and analysis; containment, eradication, and recovery; post-incident activity. NIST combines containment, eradication, and recovery into one phase; Revision 3 (April 2025) now supersedes Rev. 2.
questions.discriminator_tested: Four phases; the third combines three steps.

questions.stem: A small US company hit by major ransomware wants to report it to the federal government and get guidance. Where should it go?

options.rationale: Correct: guidance, alerts, and a place to report.

questions.explanation: CISA (Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency) provides guidance, alerts, and a place to report incidents. It is a government agency and reporting point, not a lifecycle model.

questions.stem: A company skips baselines, training, and tools, planning to figure things out when an incident happens. What is the MAIN consequence?

options.rationale: Correct: preparation is the first phase.
Fewer alerts because less is detected.

options.text: Lower costs in the long run

questions.explanation: Incident preparation means policies, a trained team, tools, baselines, and communication ready before an incident. It is the first phase and also covers prevention planning.

questions.stem: Given the risk assessment below, what should the CSIRT prepare for FIRST?
questions.exhibit:
Asset            Threat likelihood   Impact
Payment portal   High                High
Intranet wiki    Medium              Low
Print server     Low                 Low
questions.explanation: Risk assessments in preparation identify likely threats, vulnerabilities, and valuable assets to focus preparation. They drive priorities.

questions.stem: An alert shows a possible intrusion on a database server. What is the BEST next step before any containment?

options.text: Close it as a false positive

questions.explanation: Detection and analysis means detecting, validating, scoping, and prioritizing a suspected incident. It follows preparation and determines whether, and how badly, something happened.

questions.stem: Which two entries in the response log below are containment actions? (Choose two.)
questions.exhibit:
10:02  EDR: host WS-22 network-isolated
10:05  FW: blocked outbound traffic to 198.51.100.7
10:40  EDR: malware removed from WS-22
11:30  WS-22 reimaged and returned to service
14:00  Lessons-learned meeting scheduled
questions.explanation: Containment limits spread and damage: isolate hosts, block addresses, disable accounts. It stops the damage first and precedes eradication.
